title: God Is Our Refuge and Our Strength
description: God Is Our Refuge and Our Strength in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Alford wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 255, “God Our Refuge. Psalm xlvi”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God is our re-fuge and our strength, When trou-ble's hour is near; A ve-ry pre-sent help is He; There-fore we will not fear.

lines: God is our refuge and our strength,
A very present help is He;
Although the pillars of the earth
Although the waters rage and swell,
So that the earth shall shake;
Yea, and the solid mountain roots
There is a river that makes glad
The Lord is in the midst of her,
Because the Lord our God himself
The Lord our strength and refuge is,
A very present help is He;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Alford died in 1871.
credits: Words by Henry Alford (1810–1871), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
